editorial: Cambodia was fairly affordable. Our mid-August visit benefited from off-peak prices.
We recorded about $440 for two people over two nights, excluding flights into and out of Siem Reap.
We found food in Siem Reap expensive relative to what was on offer.
Stays
Pandora Suite d’Angkor, a small hotel with a pool, cost us around $30 per night. Once again, we saved money by avoiding peak season.
Food & Drinks
Food and drinks came to about $100, excluding the buffet included with the Apsara show.
We didn’t drink or party much, so our spending won’t tell you much about nightlife costs.
Experiences
We noted about $75 for Angkor passes, $28 for the guided tour and a $20 tip for our wonderful guide.
The Apsara dance and buffet cost another $70 for two, and gave us both an introduction to Cambodian tradition and our favourite meal of the trip.
Inter-City Travel
We didn’t travel between cities, but the airport bus cost $8 each, and the Grab taxi back cost $30.
Miscellaneous
Our visas were $30 each.
SIM cards would be an additional expense; we didn’t record an amount for them here.
What if we had a bigger budget?
With a bigger budget, we wouldn’t change much about this short stay — perhaps we’d tip our guide more.
What if we had a smaller budget?
With a smaller budget, we’d bring snacks to reduce meal spending and consider skipping the Apsara performance if its price felt too steep.
Budget note: The receipt’s reconstructed line items add up to about $459, so the breakdown and our recorded total differ by about $19; both are approximate trip notes, not current quotes.
